description: Experience the fiery flavors of Sichuan cuisine with this authentic Vegetarian Mapo Tofu, a beloved dish transformed into a vibrant meatless masterpiece. Silken tofu cubes are simmered in a rich, spicy sauce featuring fermented broad bean paste, Sichuan peppercorns, and chili, delivering a delightful numbing and spicy sensation. This satisfying and aromatic plant-based meal is perfect for a cozy dinner, promising a burst of traditional Chinese taste in every bite.

instructions.title: Prepare Tofu and Aromatics
instructions.text: Carefully cut the tofu into 2cm cubes. Bring a pot of water to a gentle boil, add a pinch of salt, and blanch the tofu for 2-3 minutes. This helps firm it up and remove excess moisture. Drain gently and set aside. Mince the garlic and ginger, chop the green onions separating white and green parts, and rinse the fermented black beans.

instructions.title: Infuse Chili Oil
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of neutral cooking oil in a wok or large pan over medium heat. Add the toasted and ground Sichuan peppercorns and dried red chilies. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and the chilies slightly darken. Be careful not to burn them. Remove the peppercorns and chilies if you prefer less texture, or leave them in for more intensity.

instructions.title: Sauté the Flavor Base
instructions.text: Add the white parts of the green onions, minced garlic, and minced ginger to the infused oil. Stir-fry for about 30 seconds until aromatic. Then, add the chopped doubanjiang and the rinsed, lightly mashed fermented black beans. Continue to stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, allowing the paste to release its red oil and fragrance.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tofu in Sauce
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable broth, soy sauce, and sugar. Bring the mixture to a simmer. Gently add the blanched tofu cubes to the simmering sauce, being careful not to break them. Let it simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the tofu to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce.

instructions.title: Thicken the Sauce
instructions.text: Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir and gradually add it to the simmering tofu sauce while stirring gently. Continue to stir until the sauce thickens to your desired consistency. If it becomes too thick, add a splash more vegetable broth. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the wok from heat. Stir in the sesame oil and the green parts of the chopped green onions. Gently mix everything. Transfer the Vegetarian Mapo Tofu to a serving bowl and garnish with a final sprinkle of fresh green onions or a dash of chili oil for extra heat and aroma. Serve immediately with steamed white rice.

tips: For authentic flavor, use high-quality Pixian doubanjiang (fermented broad bean paste) and fresh Sichuan peppercorns. Toasting the peppercorns just before grinding releases their full aromatic and numbing potential.
Blanching the tofu in lightly salted water before cooking helps to firm it up, remove any raw taste, and allows it to absorb the sauce flavors better without crumbling during stirring.

Serve Mapo Tofu immediately and piping hot with steamed white rice to best appreciate its complex flavors. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and reheated gently on the stovetop or microwave.
